figures.finding: From seven to eighteen a minor has limited legal capacity, and his declaration of intent (a contract among them) is valid only with his legal representative's consent, unless it brings him only a benefit; at eighteen he is of age. No earnings set-aside rule was found in the Civil Code.
figures.applies: Georgia, Civil Code arts. 12, 14 and 15, in the Legislative Herald's consolidated English text (matsne.gov.ge).

sources.said: A person who has attained the age of eighteen years shall be a person of the age of majority.
A minor from the age of seven to eighteen years shall have limited legal capacity.

In order for the declaration of intent of a person with limited legal capacity to be valid the consent of his/her legal representative shall be required, except when the person with limited legal capacity acquires a benefit from the transaction.

figures.finding: A person may enter an employment agreement on their own from 16; under 16 only with the consent of a legal representative or the custody and guardianship authority, where the work does not go against the minor's interests, development or compulsory schooling; under 14 only for activities in sport, art and culture or work in advertising. The Code defines no light work.

sources.said: The legal capacity of natural persons to enter into an employment agreement shall commence from the age of 16.

The legal capacity of minors under the age 16 to enter into an employment agreement shall derive from the consent of their legal representative or a custody/guardianship authority, unless the labour relations in question are contrary to the minor’s interests
An employment agreement with minors under the age 14 may be concluded solely for the performance of activities in the fields of sport, art, and culture, and/or to do work in advertising.

figures.finding: A child under 14 may be employed only in sport, art, culture or advertising, and any minor under 16 works only with the consent of a legal representative or the custody and guardianship authority, which once given holds for similar later work; the consent fails where the work goes against the minor's interests. From 14 to 16 a minor works at most 4 hours a day and 24 a week, from 16 to 18 at most 6 and 36 (art. 24), and no minor works at night (art. 28); the hours were first held unknown, from the ILO's profile. No hours under 14, schooling arrangement or lower age were found, and the rule speaks of employment agreements generally, so it reaches a young writer or director employed in art or culture as much as a performer (reading).

sources.said: The legal capacity of minors under the age 16 to enter into an employment agreement shall derive from the consent of their legal representative or a custody/guardianship authority

Where the consent of a minor's legal representative or custody/guardianship authority validly constitutes legal capacity to enter into an employment agreement, such consent shall be valid with respect to similar types of subsequent labour relations as well.
The duration of working time for minors from the age of 16 to 18 shall not exceed 36 hours per week, nor 6 hours per working day.
The duration of working time for minors from the age of 14 to 16 shall not exceed 24 hours per week, nor 4 hours per working day.
shall not be employed for night work.

sources.said: Article 10 − Emergence of legal capacity to enter into employment agreements and minimum employment age 1. The legal capacity of natural persons to enter into an employment agreement shall commence from the age of 16. 2. The legal capacity of minors under the age 16 to enter into an employment agreement shall derive from the consent of their legal representative or a custody/guardianship authority, unless the labour relations in question are contrary to the minor’s interests ... Where the consent of a minor's legal representative or custody/guardianship authority validly constitutes legal capacity to enter into an employment agreement, such consent shall be valid with respect to similar types of subsequent labour relations as well. 3. An employment agreement with minors under the age 14 may be concluded solely for the performance of activities in the fields of sport, art, and culture, and/or to do work in advertising. ... Article 24 ... 8. The duration of working time for minors from the age of 16 to 18 shall not exceed 36 hours per week, nor 6 hours per working day. 9. The duration of working time for minors from the age of 14 to 16 shall not exceed 24 hours per week, nor 4 hours per working day. ... Article 28 ... 3. Minors ... shall not be employed for night work.
